claim_1.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of platelet-rich plasma from young, Older (Comm), and Older (SNF) adults at Day 0 showed an age-associated increase in platelet activation RNAs and mitochondrial genes, and a decrease in translation-related RNAs.

sources.section: Platelets in older adults are characterized by pre‐vaccination increased platelet activation and decreased translation pathways
sources.quote: Overall, pre‐vaccination RNA expression variability was most highly associated with group membership, and there was a continuum of transcriptional states moving from Young to Older (Comm) to Older (SNF) adults.

sources.section: Platelets in older adults are characterized by pre‐vaccination increased platelet activation and decreased translation pathways
sources.quote: These findings indicate an age‐associated increase in expression of platelet activation RNAs and mitochondrial genes and a decrease in expression of RNAs encoding translation‐related proteins.

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of platelet-rich plasma from young, Older (Comm), and Older (SNF) adults at Day 0, 2, and 7 post-vaccination showed increased surface expression of CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (Comm) compared to young adults, with decreased expression in Older (SNF) compared to Older (Comm).

sources.section: Effects of age and SNF residence on platelet activation at the protein level and comparison with expression of activation marker RNAS following vaccination
sources.quote: The levels of surface expression of all three proteins were significantly increased in platelets from Older (Comm), compared to young adults at day 0, 2, and 7, suggesting an age‐associated increase in platelet activation.

claim_3.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of serum from young and older adults at Day 0 and 28 post-vaccination showed classification of high and low vaccine responders using maxRBA, with differential RNA expression in high responders pre-vaccination.

sources.section: Platelets in older adults are characterized by pre‐vaccination increased platelet activation and decreased translation pathways
sources.quote: Influenza vaccine antibody response was measured using a standard hemagglutination inhibition assay (HAI).

sources.section: Platelets in older adults are characterized by pre‐vaccination increased platelet activation and decreased translation pathways
sources.quote: maxRBA was used to classify high and low vaccine responders for assessment of platelet transcriptomic differences in vaccine responsiveness.
